QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_12

question.text: A long-short Cat III fund's monthly excess returns over Nifty 50 for the year are: +1.0%, -0.5%, +2.0%, +0.8%, -1.2%, +1.5%, +0.3%, -0.8%, +1.2%, +0.5%, -0.4%, +0.6%. The mean excess return is +0.4167%. The standard deviation of these monthly excess returns is approximately 0.96%. What is the ANNUALISED Tracking Error?

explanation.text: The Logic: Tracking Error is the standard deviation of a fund's excess returns over its benchmark. To annualise a monthly tracking-error figure, the square-root-of-time rule (assuming iid monthly excess returns) is applied: Annualised TE = monthly TE × √12 = 0.96% × 3.464 ≈ 3.33%. TE quantifies how tightly the fund tracks (or diverges from) its benchmark and is a standard input alongside Information Ratio in active-management reporting. The Trap: 0.96% is the un-annualised monthly TE. 11.52% multiplies by 12 instead of √12 (forgetting the variance-scales-linearly rule). 5.00% is fabricated and does not correspond to any of the standard transformations. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (166, 191-193) cover related risk metrics — standard deviation, Sharpe, Treynor, beta — but do not define Tracking Error or its √12 annualisation. The formula and framing above are general industry/quantitative-finance knowledge rather than a workbook-page citation.
